expert_search_strategy_decision_before_r.next_search_hypothesis: The progress-delta reward and no-op penalty from iter_001 successfully incentivized main engine usage and approach behavior, but the reward still has two critical flaws: (1) the success bonus fires in non-terminal states (both legs contact + distance < 0.15) creating proxy-success farming without true terminal success, and (2) the crash penalty heuristic (both legs not in contact -> crash) misclassifies normal flight as crashes, penalizing exploration. The next edit should: (a) make the success bonus truly terminal-aligned by only paying when the episode terminates with both legs contact, near pad, low vertical speed, and upright orientation, (b) fix the crash penalty to only apply on actual environment termination (game_over or out-of-bounds), not on leg contact state, (c) preserve the progress-delta reward and near-pad bonus as non-terminal guidance, (d) increase the main engine bonus to +0.5 when distance > 0.5 to provide stronger incentive for approach, and (e) add diagnostics for success_flag and objective_bonus to enable post-training audits. The expected behavior change is that the policy will learn to complete the landing task (success_like_terminal_rate > 0.0) instead of farming proxy-success rewards.

The negative edges indicate that removing non-terminal positive incentives (iter_002) or keeping a flawed crash penalty heuristic (iter_003) are both harmful. The next edit must preserve the progress-delta and near-pad guidance from iter_001 while fixing the success bonus to be terminal-aligned and the crash penalty to only apply on actual environment termination. The main engine bonus should be increased to provide stronger approach incentive.
